strings.name: Evo Morales
strings.summary: From an Aymara farming family, Morales entered politics through coca-growers’ unions and governed Bolivia from 2006 to 2019, widely regarded as its first indigenous president. He strengthened state control of gas and advanced a new constitution, while facing criticism over prolonged rule and reelection. He resigned and went into exile amid the 2019 electoral crisis, later returning. In 2026 he faced trafficking-related and protest-related proceedings, which he disputed.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Widely regarded as Bolivia’s first indigenous president, he advanced resource nationalization and constitutional reform, while his political movement has had enduring influence in the Andes.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Rural Isallawi in the Orinoca area of Oruro, Bolivia.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Received basic schooling and performed military service, later growing coca and organizing unions in Chapare.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Resource and constitutional reform
strings.highlights.h1.text: Advanced state control of gas and the 2009 constitution, increasing indigenous visibility in national politics.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Reelection and legal controversies
strings.highlights.h2.text: Resigned after the disputed 2019 election; warrants and proceedings in 2026 must be distinguished from convictions.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Prosecutors ordered another arrest
strings.timeline.t1.text: Prosecutors issued another warrant over alleged conduct during 2026 protests and roadblocks; it was not a conviction.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Trafficking-related trial suspended
strings.timeline.t2.text: After his failure to appear, a judge suspended the trial pending arrest or appearance; he denied the allegations.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Resigned as president
strings.timeline.t3.text: Left office amid a disputed election, protests and a military call to resign, subsequently going into exile.
strings.timeline.t4.title: New constitution took effect
strings.timeline.t4.text: Advanced a referendum-approved constitution establishing a plurinational state and revised indigenous-rights framework.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Announced gas nationalization
strings.timeline.t5.text: Increased state control over natural gas resources and contracts with foreign firms.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Became Bolivian president
strings.timeline.t6.text: Took office after winning the 2005 election, beginning a presidency lasting until 2019.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Elected to Congress
strings.timeline.t7.text: Moved from the coca-growers’ union movement into the national legislature.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Developed coca-growers’ union work
strings.timeline.t8.text: Organized with coca-growers’ unions in Chapare and gradually took leadership posts.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Returned to Bolivia from exile
strings.timeline.t9.text: Crossed the border from Argentina after Luis Arce’s inauguration as president.
